content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes channel fusion to learn cross-modal representations of image-text pairs. Channel fusion combines co-attention (cross-attention) and merged attention mechanisms. It first uses cross-attention to obtain compound tokens, which are then fed into merged attention. The paper conducts experiments on downstream vision-language tasks including VQA, GQA, SNLI-VE and achieves competitive performance on GQA and SNLI-VE.
content.strength_and_weaknesses: The proposed method is simple and achieves competitive performance on GQA and SNLI-VE.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
1. The improvements in ablation studies compared with co-attention and merged attention are marginal (0.2-0.3 on SNLI-VE). Although the improvement on VQA is almost 4 points, the performance of the baseline is just 53, which is very weak compared with SoTA models. I have concerns about whether this small change will bring improvements on some stronger baselines.
2. I feel confused about why only using cross-attention w/o using self-attention for learning compound tokens. The motivation for combing co-attention and merged attention is also not clear to me.
3. A small error in the caption of Figure 1. "(a) co-attention (b) merged attention". It seems that (a) is merged attention and (b) is co-attention?
content.summary_of_the_review: The proposed method is simple. But my main concern is the relatively small improvement and the unclear motivation for combing co-attention and merged attention.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper introduces compound tokens that fuse vision and language tokens by using cross-attention and channel concatenation.  Experiments are conducted on three benchmark datasets to demonstrate the proposed method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
1. The present figure clearly shows the proposed method and its differences from other designs.
2. The experimental results show that the proposed method is a bit better than the other two designs.

Weaknesses
1. The improvement of the present method is not significant. In Table 3, the compound method performs similarly to other methods. 
2. The efficiency of the proposed design is not clear. In figure 2, There are N visual tokens and M word tokens, the outputs are still (M + N) tokens. Compared to merge attention, more parameters are involved. Why does the proposed model cost fewer FLOPS?
3. The evaluation task only contains the QA task, more tasks should be included to demonstrate the proposed method.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The method is intuitively present in both the figure and content.  The effectiveness of the present method is  not significant and its efficiency is unclear.
content.summary_of_the_review: The technique contribution of the introduced method is a bit weak and the experiments are insufficient. I tend to reject the current version.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper provides a new method of fusing vision and language representations for primarily questions answering tasks. The primary idea seems to be fusion paradigm where the attended inputs from the other modality are concatenated in the feature dimension and then fed to the more common transformer networks. The overall idea is simple, and the experimental results show that it might bring in some improvements when incorporated into the SOTA techniques.
content.strength_and_weaknesses: The primary strength of the paper is the very point that simple alignment differences with stronger embeddings can improve the SOTA vision language methods. The core proposition in Eq. 2 and 3. modify the inputs to standard multi-modal transformer-based architectures. I am primarily concerned with the novelty of the technique, where the cross-attention models have been shown to improve transformer performance in many different settings. Cross attention being concatenated in the feature domain is a new way to look into this fusion but whether this modification is significant enough might need more experimentation.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: The paper is clearly written and conveys it primary ideas well. 

Quality/Novelty: the ideas presented in this work seem to work well. My primary concern is the novelty as well as lack of experiments on multi-modal benchmarks and tasks. The authors first propose an encoder-decoder based model and then suddenly switch to an encoder only model for VQA. The competitive SOTA papers present results on image-text retrievals which constitutes an important part of metric for evaluating vision language models. The lack of such experimentation in this paper stands out. 

Given the simplicity of the idea, I believe the reproducibility should not be of concern.
content.summary_of_the_review: I think the authors point to an important aspect of the multi-modal fusion problem wherein the feature dimension itself can be augmented on. That being said, the other parts of the paper do not provide a very good understanding of why such a fusion should work and provides a relatively smaller set of experiments to validate the claims.

content.title: Compound Tokens: Channel Fusion for Vision-Language Representation Learning
content.TL;DR: We provide a new multi-modal fusion method that concatenates tokens along the channel dimension.
content.abstract:
We present an effective method for fusing visual-and-language representations for several question answering tasks including visual question answering and visual entailment.
In contrast to prior works that concatenate unimodal representations or use only cross-attention, we compose multimodal representations via channel fusion. By fusing on the channels, the model is able to more effectively align the tokens compared to standard methods. These multimodal representations, which we call compound tokens are generated with cross-attention transformer layers. First, vision tokens are used as queries to retrieve compatible text tokens through cross-attention. We then chain the vision tokens and the queried text tokens along the channel dimension. We call the resulting representations compound tokens. A second group of compound tokens are generated using an analogous process where the text tokens serve as queries to the cross-attention layer. We concatenate all the compound tokens for further processing with multimodal encoder.  We demonstrate the effectiveness of compound tokens using an encoder-decoder vision-language model trained end-to-end in the open-vocabulary setting. Compound Tokens achieve highly competitive performance across a range of question answering tasks including GQA, VQA2.0, and  SNLI-VE.
We plan to make the code public.
